name: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure Ltd
title: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure Ltd - 544335 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY26 revenue up 61% to INR820 crore and EBITDA margin 9.13%, but order book fell to INR1,235 crore from INR1,313 crore and no capacity or capex discipline signals were given.

triggers.label: Order book down to INR1,235 cr

triggers.label: Growth target 20-25% FY27
triggers.quote: the approach is to maintain a growth of 20% to 25% every year.

triggers.label: Shift to toll (TOT) and BOT bids
triggers.quote: the government has started BOT models again, where I am trying to reach the BOT model.

guidance.quote: we expect around a 20% to 25% growth rate, trying to maintain that.
instead of 9% our target is 10% to 11% target for the current year.

red_flags.quote: we have observed a year -on-year marginal decrease in your order book.

red_flags.quote: the problem with wastewater is right now that we don't have credentials. So, we are doing it on a subcontracting basis

red_flags.quote: you will see the operating cash flow was negative at that time because execution was done

we haven't made the position for 31st May of the current year yet

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR820 crore and PAT rose 77.8% to INR44.92 crore; order book stood at about INR1,235 crore at 31 March 2026.
summary.overview: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure reported FY26 revenue from operations up 61% YoY to INR820 crore, with EBITDA (excluding other income) up about 82% to INR75 crore and EBITDA margin up 105 bps to 9.13%. H2 FY26 revenue was INR478 crore (up 61% YoY) with EBITDA of INR47.48 crore at a 9.93% margin. Management said the order book declined YoY to about INR1,235 crore, which it attributed to bidding for larger-ticket projects and faster execution. The company also flagged a preferential warrant issue of up to INR13.09 crore, higher borrowing limits, a maiden dividend of INR0.25 per share, and entry into wastewater civil works.

segments.name: EPC (roads, buildings, urban)
segments.commentary: Management cited an EPC EBITDA margin of about 14% for FY26 (13-15% range), up from 12-13% last year. FY26 revenue split by business: road/EPC about 49%, RMC about 3%, toll collection about 47%. Sector revenue cited: road/building EPC about INR395 crore, RMC about INR20 crore, wastewater about INR6 crore, toll about INR388 crore.

segments.name: Toll collection contracts (TCC)
segments.commentary: Toll EBITDA margin about 4% in FY26 (about 3% last year); management also cited a toll segment margin of about 2.5%. Toll strike rate is above 70%. Recent NHAI toll awards include Kathpur INR91.71 crore, Simliya INR86.7 crore, Aashpur INR70.39 crore, Khambara INR47.83 crore, Paraghat INR33.27 crore.

segments.name: Wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Entered in FY26 with a Tamil Nadu project of about INR167 crore; wastewater order book about INR162 crore. Management cited a 15-20% EBITDA margin for the vertical, but work is currently subcontracted or on name-lending basis with no technology tie-up. Target contribution of 20-25% of revenue in the near future.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete and real estate
segments.commentary: RMC revenue about INR20 crore in FY26. Residential plotting in Indore has about 1.8 lakh sq ft unsold inventory, with WIP/inventory about INR15 crore. The company also holds a 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP, a Indore commercial real-estate build with about 3-3.5 lakh sq ft saleable area and expected revenue of about INR150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 20-25% revenue growth annually; for FY27 it aims for EBITDA margin of 10-11% against 9.13% in FY26 (about 9-9.25% blended in its margin discussion).
Top FY27 priority is order inflow of about INR2,000 crore, across roads, wastewater and toll contracts.
Bids of about INR1,500-2,000 crore are pending opening; about INR2,500 crore of orders identified for bidding in the current month.
Bid capacity cited at about INR2,000 crore; individual EPC bid capacity INR600-700 crore; building about INR150 crore; toll collection described as unlimited based on net worth.
Plans to bid PPP, HAM and BOT projects in the current fiscal, including NHAI asset monetisation of about 17 road projects.
Management said it would not commit to the projected INR1,000-1,200 crore of project completions in FY27.
capex_capacity: Equipment base of 230+ construction equipment and vehicles; workforce above 1,100 employees.
Operates 37 ongoing projects across nine states; executed more than 40 projects in total.
Preferential issue of convertible warrants up to INR13.09 crore approved; proceeds targeted at working capital needs in about 10-12 months.
Borrowing limits enhancement proposed to support larger projects.
Acquired 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP (Indore real-estate build, completion in about 2-2.5 years).
demand_pricing: Management said tender flow has not slowed; the YoY order book decline reflects a shift to larger projects and faster execution of earlier orders, with about INR811 crore executed in FY26.
Strike rate: about 10-15% in EPC road building and above 70% in toll collection contracts.
Wastewater competition is intensifying: for a INR200 crore BUIDCO bid there were 15-20 bidders; the company was L2 in one and L3 in another bid.
Fuel and crude price volatility: force majeure and price-escalation clauses are being invoked; management says a short-term hit of about 1-1.5 months has since stabilised.
Company prefers centrally funded projects (NHAI, NHIDCL, MoRTH); working capital cycle cited at 30-45 days.
Company prefers large tickets: NH projects above INR500 crore and building projects above INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall YoY, and is tender flow slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no slowdown; the company is bidding for larger projects and executed INR811 crore in FY26 against a INR1,313 crore opening order book. It said about INR1,500-2,000 crore has been bid and is not yet opened.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should investors expect going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended EBITDA margin is 9-9.25% currently; FY26 toll EBITDA was about 4% and EPC about 14%. Target for the current year is 10-11% blended.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wastewater margin, and how will mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Wastewater EBITDA margin was cited at 15-20%. Management expects wastewater at about 20-25% of revenue in the near future, with the balance from roads, buildings, RMC and toll. It is currently subcontracting or name-lending because it lacks credentials.

qa_highlights.question: How did FY26 growth split across business lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 revenue split of about 49% road, 3% RMC, 47% toll, with wastewater very small. Road and toll drove the growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to fuel price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts include force majeure and price-variation provisions; some agencies have issued SOPs, and the company expects price variations to offset the increase.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest opportunities and risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Opportunities cited are large TOT-model toll contracts of INR1,500-2,000 crore and the return of BOT projects. Execution risk remains, though management said it has 40 years of experience and works in nine states.

risks_watch: Order book fell YoY to about INR1,235 crore; conversion of about INR1,500-2,000 crore pending bids is key to FY27 growth.
Wastewater margin claims (15-20%) are unproven; the company lacks credentials and works as subcontractor or name-lender; competition is intense.
Management declined to commit to FY27 completions of INR1,000-1,200 crore, citing geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
Toll segment margin (about 2.5-4%) is much lower than EPC, so mix shift toward toll dilutes margin.
Operating cash flow was negative in FY25 and turned positive in FY26; sustainability is management's expectation, not guaranteed.
Management did not provide an order book figure as of 31 May 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin direction, but evasive on specifics: management declined to commit to FY27 project completion figures and offered inconsistent segment margin and revenue-mix figures. Answers on wastewater and PPP/HAM strategy were broad and aspirational.
key_quotes: Sir, we expect around a 20% to 25% growth rate, trying to maintain that.
So, we are trying to stay around 40% in EPC road and building from revenue.
We don't think we are conservative in out bidding we think we shouldn't unnecessarily have an order book of INR5,000 crores and then not be able to execute the work for 5, 10 years.

growth.why: Management guides 20-25% revenue growth annually for FY27 (midpoint 22.5%) and a 10-11% EBITDA margin versus 9.13% in FY26, backed by a ~INR1,235 crore order book, bid capacity of ~INR2,000 crore and pending bids of INR1,500-2,000 crore, but no new productive capacity is added and management declined to commit to the INR1,000-1,200 crore FY27 completions.
